title: Machine learning on serum proteomics predicts 10-year risk of metabolic syndrome
summary: Over 400 proteins were measured by mass spectrometry in 7,890 serum samples from a longitudinal cohort of 3,840 participants. A machine-learning model of 11 proteins plus age predicted metabolic syndrome within 10 years with an AUC of 0.774 in a validation cohort (n=242). Apolipoproteins, immune-related and coagulation-related proteins correlated best with disease development; the abstract does not state whether the validation cohort was independent of the training data.
ai_technology: Machine-learning model on serum proteomic data to predict metabolic syndrome risk

evidence.tested: Prediction of 10-year metabolic syndrome risk in a validation cohort of 242 participants.
evidence.unknown: Independence of the validation cohort and clinical utility; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning built the risk-prediction model from serum proteins and age.
